teams.heading: Jake White will move to live in Fiji from early 2027
teams.body: Fiji head coach Jake White, who started last month, is all-in: he will move to live in Fiji in early 2027 and spend blocks of each year touring the islands, and plans to coach in schools and clubs. He beat strong competition for the role, and says timing won it for him. He also says no one in Fiji coaches the maul. The Fiji U18s and U20s will start touring South Africa every year.

lead.why: It is the day's freshest Fiji-specific item, a new interview with the head coach on his plans, and it outranks the recycled Higgins piece and Ireland-side previews.

teams.heading: Borthwick overhauls England for Japan, with Ojomoh and Pollock starting
teams.body: England named a much-changed side on Friday for Saturday's Japan match at Twickenham, with Steve Borthwick making ten personnel and two positional changes from the team that beat Australia 45-22. Max Ojomoh returns at 12 in his first England appearance since man of the match against Argentina a year ago, and Henry Pollock, who scored twice off the bench against Australia, starts at No. 8. Guardian rugby writer Robert Kitson called it a "use-it-or-lose-it" selection for players eyeing next year's World Cup in Australia.

lead.why: A fresh team selection with a clear England angle, and the one most fans would discuss.

teams.heading: Antoine Dupont's France hold on to beat South Africa 21-19
teams.body: Friday's Nations Championship thriller at Stade de France ended a five-match losing run against the Springboks on home soil. Injuries to fly-halves Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack and Antoine Hastoy left France coach Fabien Galthie with little option but to pick captain Antoine Dupont in the 10 shirt, although he played at scrum-half. Théo Attissogbe, Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang and Louis Bielle-Biarrey scored in a frantic first half, and Dupont was named player of the match. The win leaves France six points clear at the top of the northern hemisphere standings.

lead.why: A fresh result against the world champions, with France's captain central to how the win came about.

teams.heading: Dan Sheehan and Sean Jansen injuries force changes to Ireland's XV against Fiji
teams.body: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell made seven changes for Saturday's Nations Championship match against Fiji at the Aviva Stadium, two of them forced by injuries to Dan Sheehan and Sean Jansen. Jamison Gibson-Park is restored to the starting XV, while Joe McCarthy and Hugo Keenan were rested from the match-day 23. The replacements are James Ryan and Tommy O'Brien, and Farrell wants a bonus-point win to build momentum before South Africa visit Dublin next weekend.

teams.heading: Giacomo Nicotera admits Italy's performance against South Africa was not enough
teams.body: Italy captain Giacomo Nicotera, speaking at the pre-Argentina press conference, said the squad had been strongly self-critical after the heavy defeat to South Africa in Turin. He pointed to aerial play, defence, organisation and discipline, with too many penalties conceded under South Africa's breakdown pressure, and described a hard Monday review that demanded a more intense response in training. Italy then lost 14-19 to Argentina in Genoa on Saturday.

lead.why: It is the freshest Italy item on the shortlist, and it gives the captain's own verdict on the South Africa defeat.

teams.heading: Midlothian five-year-old who overcame brain tumour delivers Scotland match ball
teams.body: A young fan who has come through a brain tumour spent time with the Scotland squad before delivering the match ball. The five-year-old from Midlothian was buzzing to meet the players, and his visit lands on the day Scotland face Australia at Murrayfield. For a squad about to take the field, it is the kind of moment that puts the jersey in perspective.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy's Wales answer All Blacks haka with red-lit 'Dragon's Breath' display
teams.body: Wales head coach Steve Tandy's side answered the All Blacks' haka before Saturday's Nations Championship match at the Principality Stadium. As the lights dimmed, New Zealand were picked out in a single spotlight; Wales were then bathed in deep red light and surrounded by smoke, a display the Welsh Rugby Union labelled the 'Dragon's Breath'. It recalled 1905, when Wales answered the haka with the Welsh National Anthem at Cardiff Arms Park. Fans online were quick to praise the lighting and choreography.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi's Pumas face a heavily depleted France after Italy win
teams.body: Argentina head into Round 6 of the Nations Championship off a 19-14 win over Italy, and Rugbyrama reports that France, though heavily depleted, are still determined to get a result. The Pumas are described as being in a tough spot after a difficult year. The last meeting, in November 2024, went France's way 37-23, and Argentina's most recent win in the fixture came in 2014, when Nicolás Sánchez kicked four drop goals.

teams.heading: Les Kiss restores Carter Gordon and Rob Valetini to Wallabies starting XV
teams.body: Playmaker Carter Gordon, back from a broken leg, and back-rower Rob Valetini are named in the starting XV for Scotland, with coach Les Kiss saying of Valetini, "He’s going to make a difference, that’s for sure." Gordon was the incumbent before his injury against Argentina in September, and Kiss sees him as the man to nail down a No 10 jersey that has gone to seven different starting flyhalves since the last World Cup. Valetini returns to No 6 alongside Harry Wilson and Fraser McReight.

lead.why: A fresh team-selection event for the Scotland test, and the only NEW item on the shortlist about Australia's own team.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones vows Japan will 'play the house down' against England
teams.body: Japan head coach Eddie Jones, who spent 2015 to 2022 in charge of England, has vowed his side will 'play the house down' at Allianz Stadium on Saturday. The challenge carries weight for a Japan side facing England, who have never lost to Japan and scored a half-century of points in each of their two most recent meetings, according to the Guardian.

teams.heading: Frank Bunce says he couldn't name Wales players ahead of Cardiff Test
teams.body: Wales have been poor for more than a couple of years, former All Blacks centre Frank Bunce told Sport Nation. "I couldn't name any of their players to be honest," he said. "I think the All Blacks will beat them and beat them well whichever team we put out there." All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie made eight changes to his starting XV for the Principality Stadium Test, with fly-half Richie Mo'unga among those coming in.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus puts Paris defeat on Springboks, not referee Andrea Piardi
teams.body: Head coach Rassie Erasmus accepted responsibility after Friday's Nations Championship defeat in Paris, saying the team was tentative and the coaching staff should answer for it. He spent his press conference describing the pressure referee Andrea Piardi faces before a partisan crowd, but said he was not criticising him. "I don't think there's much more to blame than ourselves," he said. France led 21-7 at the break, and the Boks, despite two maul tries, fell two points short.

lead.why: Erasmus's post-match press conference is a fresh, quotable item that none of the earlier editions covered.
